pages.title: Introduction
pages.content:
## What is this?

Steamworks Power is the industry add-on of Steamworks: five machines that make a factory out of a river and a lot of patience. They run on the same rotation network as every other Steamworks part - same shafts, same stress, same wrench.

### The machines

* **Water Turbine** - a brass drum that sits in river current and turns it into strong, steady rotation. The quiet cousin of the water wheel: less noise, more torque.
* **Mechanical Press** - a brass arch that stamps whatever lies on top of it. Nine zinc nuggets become a clean ingot; four snow blocks become dense ice. The press does what the furnace can't.
* **Stock Ticker** - a small copper counter that leans against a chest or barrel and shows, on a floating plate, what is inside and how much of it.
* **Brass Flywheel** - a heavy wheel on the line. It winds itself up while the power runs; when the power falls away it takes over and coasts the machines through the dip, until its charge runs out.
* **Sieve Funnel** - a funnel with a brass mesh at the end of a belt line. Show it one item and only that item falls into the container below; everything else is tossed off the side.

### In the game

* All five craft at the workbench and show up in `/zukan` and the [recipes page](/recipes).
* They need rotation, not fuel: hook a turbine or steam engine up to the network and the press works while the network runs.
* Staff hand out parts with `/swpower give <player> <machine>`; `/swpower list` shows what exists.

### Good to know

* The press is a working surface: items land on top, the ram stamps them, the results drop beside it. A funnel or hopper minecart underneath keeps the line running.
* The stock ticker does not rotate - it reads containers. Place it against a chest, barrel, or any Steamworks machine that holds items.
* The water turbine wants its full drum surrounded: water touching the sides, the shaft going through the ends. In a millrace that is exactly what you build anyway.
* The flywheel doesn't care which source charges it - river, wind or steam. Right-click it to see how full it is. It only takes over when the line actually stops.
* The sieve funnel sorts items, not fluids. Right-click it empty to check its filter, sneak right-click empty to open it up again.

[Power & the turbine](/wiki?page=power-turbine) · [Press & ticker](/wiki?page=power-machines)

pages.title: The Water Turbine
pages.content:
## The Water Turbine

A copper drum on an axle, big enough to hide a shaft and small enough for a town canal. Where a water wheel needs a broad river, a turbine is happy in a two-block millrace.


* [What it does](/wiki?page=power-turbine-what-it-does)
* [Building with it](/wiki?page=power-turbine-building-with-it)
* [Crafting](/wiki?page=power-turbine-crafting)
* [Placing and moving](/wiki?page=power-turbine-placing-and-moving)

pages.title: What it does
pages.content:
* It sits on the shaft line: rotation enters and leaves through both ends, like any shaft part. The drum must feel **water on its sides**.
* A **flowing** side gives it full power (12 RPM, 64 torque per RPM = 768 Tq); only still water on both sides gives half. Two flowing sides add a quarter on top.
* The turbine produces; it never consumes. Hook it up and it drives the whole line it touches.

Back to [The Water Turbine](/wiki?page=power-turbine)

pages.title: Building with it
pages.content:
Dig a race: water flows in beside the drum, the tailrace flows out on the other side. The turbine keeps turning as long as the water next to it **moves** - so a waterfall that lands on the drum works; a stagnant pond doesn't.

A canal town can hide these under every bridge: nobody sees a wheel, everybody enjoys the torque.

Back to [The Water Turbine](/wiki?page=power-turbine)

pages.title: Crafting
pages.content:
**4 iron ingots** (corners), **2 brass casings** (left and right) and **1 propeller** (center) → 1 Water Turbine.

The propeller is the expensive bit: two copper plates around a steel hub, and Steamworks' own - the press and the turbine share one family of parts.

Back to [The Water Turbine](/wiki?page=power-turbine)

pages.title: Placing and moving
pages.content:
Right-click a shaft end to place it, sneak right-click to pull it back (like any network part). Sneak-right-click with a wrench to turn it into your hand. The turbine itself does not store items or fluids.

Staff: `/swpower give <player> pow_water_turbine`.

Back to [The Water Turbine](/wiki?page=power-turbine)

pages.title: Mechanical Press
pages.content:
A brass arch over a heavy ram. Items that lie **on top** of the press get stamped while it turns; the results fall out beside it. The press does not smelt - it **compacts**: nuggets to ingots, snow to ice, clay to bricks, and it gives the honey back its bottle.

* Needs rotation from below: a shaft enters through the bottom, like a millstone.
* Work speed depends on the network (full speed ≈ 3 s per item at 12 RPM).
* The recipe list lives in the plugin's `config.yml` under `press:` - server owners add their own compacting recipes; `/swpower reload` applies them.

Defaults:

| On the plate | In the box below |
|---|---|
| 9 Zinc Nuggets | 1 Zinc Ingot |
| 1 Honey Bottle | 1 Glass Bottle (+ 25% Honeycomb) |
| 1 Clay block | 4 Bricks |
| 1 Hay Block | 1 Leather (+ returns the hay, 50%) |
| 4 Snow Blocks | 2 Packed Ice |

Craft: **iron plates** over an andesite casing, piston and two iron ingots as the legs.

Staff: `/swpower give <player> pow_mechanical_press`.

Back to [Press, Ticker, Flywheel & Sieve](/wiki?page=power-machines)

pages.title: Stock Ticker
pages.content:
A copper box with two little dials that **counts the container it leans against**: chest, barrel, hopper, or a Steamworks tank. Above it floats the two biggest stacks ("Cobblestone x128 | Flint x40 · 23/27") - visible from across the yard, only while players are near.

* No rotation needed. Place it against any block with an inventory; if several touch, it picks the nearest.
* Right-click: a one-line summary of the container in your action bar.
* Craft: glass panes around a comparator, on a brass casing.

Staff: `/swpower give <player> pow_stock_ticker`.

Back to [Press, Ticker, Flywheel & Sieve](/wiki?page=power-machines)

pages.title: Brass Flywheel
pages.content:
A heavy brass wheel on a steel axle. While the network runs it stores the spin; when the power source falls away - the river drops, the boiler dies, someone pulls the clutch - the wheel **takes the line over** and keeps every machine turning at a slowly falling speed until its charge is spent.

* It charges from whatever turns the line: turbine, engine, windmill, all the same to it - anything at 3 RPM or more. Even a hand crank winds it, as long as someone keeps turning.
* Right-click it: the action bar shows the charge in percent and what it is doing (winding up / full / running down).
* Real power coming back simply hands the wheel the line over again; nothing is lost.
* The last stretch sputters - a nearly empty wheel coasts the line at a crawl instead of snapping it.

Craft: **four brass plates** bolted around a **brass casing**.

Staff: `/swpower give <player> pow_brass_flywheel`.

Back to [Press, Ticker, Flywheel & Sieve](/wiki?page=power-machines)

pages.title: Sieve Funnel
pages.content:
A brass mesh on four steel legs, sitting at the end of a belt or chute line. Right-click it **with any item** and the mesh tunes itself to exactly that item: matching items fall into the container underneath, everything else is tossed off the side and the line keeps running.

* The filter reads the item itself, not just its material: two different Steamworks plates with the same head are two different filters.
* Right-click empty: what does the mesh currently hold? Sneak right-click empty: open the mesh - everything passes.
* No filter and no container below? Items wait on the line - nothing is voided.
* It sifts items, not fluids, and never turns: it is a static piece of the line, like the funnel it is built from.

Craft: **two iron plates** and a **string** for the mesh frame, around your old faithful **funnel**.

Staff: `/swpower give <player> pow_sieve_funnel`.

Back to [Press, Ticker, Flywheel & Sieve](/wiki?page=power-machines)

pages.title: Taking them back
pages.content:
Left-click twice, like every Steamworks part: the machine drops as an item (creative: one sneak right-click with the wrench).

Back to [Press, Ticker, Flywheel & Sieve](/wiki?page=power-machines)
